events.text: The Ministry of Stars sends its charts round the Isles, as it does every century, and this time there is a hole in them. A quarter of the sky that astronomers have counted for ten thousand years has a gap in it, round and dark, like a missing tooth. The covering note is very calm. The handwriting is not.

choices.text: Sit with the charts until you understand the gap

effects.log: You sit three nights. The gap is not empty. It is full of something that has eaten the light.

choices.text: Take the charts to the Jade Court yourself

effects.log: The Court thanks you and files them. A minister catches your sleeve afterwards and asks, very quietly, what you saw.

choices.text: Roll the charts up and put them away

effects.log: You put them away. That night you dream of a mouth the size of a sky.

events.text: A miner from the lower isles comes to your landing with a spirit stone wrapped in silk. The vein it came from has gone grey and cold overnight, he says, and the stone hums. You hold it to your ear. It hums one note, low and patient, as if it were waiting for a door to open somewhere below the clouds.

choices.text: Hold the stone and listen to the note

effects.log: You listen until the note is inside your own qi. It is not a kind note. You learn its shape.

choices.text: Drop it into the Cloud Sea

effects.log: It falls without a splash. The miner bows, relieved, and goes home lighter.

choices.text: Send it to the Ministry alchemists

effects.log: The alchemists write back in a week: they have more like it, from every vein near the Stair.

events.text: The message cranes that carry letters between the Isles start coming in from the {og_passage} with empty tubes. They will not fly back down. By the end of the month there are hundreds of them on the roofs of the Ministry Isles, standing in rows, facing away from the Stair like a crowd that has seen an accident.

choices.text: Feed the cranes, and let them stay

effects.log: They eat from your hand. One of them stays on your roof for years afterwards.

choices.text: Fly down the Stair yourself to look

effects.log: You go down a thousand steps and stop. The air below is the wrong colour. You come back with a cold you cannot shake.

choices.text: Shoo them off, and send your letters by barge

effects.log: The barges are slower. Your letters arrive, and you hear the news a little later than everyone else.

events.text: Warden Lan Ji of the Ninefold Watch has kept the top of the {og_passage} for nine hundred years, and she asks you, of all people, to stand a night watch with her. At the third hour you hear it: a knock, from the underside of the Stair, the wrong side, slow and polite. Lan Ji does not move. 'It has done that for a month,' she says.

choices.text: Knock back

effects.log: You knock. The knocking stops. Lan Ji looks at you as if you had signed something.

choices.text: Stay still and watch the dark

effects.log: You watch till dawn. Nothing comes. You both pretend this is good news.

choices.text: Go to the Ministries with her report

effects.log: Lan Ji has sent nine reports. Yours is the first one anyone reads.

events.text: On one night a thousand immortals of the Isles have the same dream: a city of gold with no one in it, eating itself street by street, very slowly, because there is nothing else left to eat. The Jade Court calls a quiet session in the morning. Nobody says the word 'dream'. Everybody is pale.

choices.text: Speak at the session, and say what you saw

effects.log: You speak plainly. It helps the others to say it too. The session runs till dark.

choices.text: Write the dream down, every street of it

effects.log: You write it all. Years later, the Ministries will want your pages.

choices.text: Go home and sleep in the sun

effects.log: You sleep in the sun all afternoon, and do not dream at all.

events.text: The tides of the Cloud Sea come in an hour late, then two, then a whole day. The old cloud-ferryman at your landing has worked these currents since before your grandteacher was born, and he puts his oar down and says the sea is leaning. 'Leaning away from something,' he says. 'The way a dog leans from a stranger.'

choices.text: Ride out with him and feel the current

effects.log: The current pulls away from the Stair, steady as a held breath. You feel it in your meridians for a week.

choices.text: Pay him in qi-pills to keep watch for you

effects.log: He takes the pills and keeps a careful log. It fills faster than either of you would like.

choices.text: Tell him the sea has moods, like anyone

effects.log: He nods, and does not believe you, and neither do you.

events.text: At the dawn bell the {og_passage} groans like a ship's hull. A crack opens down the middle of it, a thousand steps long, and through it rises a grey that is not cloud. The Ninefold Watch run past your landing in their white coats, too fast to bow. Behind them the bell keeps ringing, and nobody remembers to stop it.

choices.text: Run with the Watch toward the crack

effects.log: You reach the top landing as the first grey shapes climb out. You help hold it for an hour. It is the longest hour of your long life.

choices.text: Clear the lower landings of their people

effects.log: You fill three barges with ferrymen and tea-sellers. Every one of them will remember your face.

choices.text: Seal your own hall and its arrays

effects.log: Your arrays hold. From behind them you hear the Isles change.

events.text: Grey rain falls on the Lotus Isles. Where it touches, colour leaves: the peonies in the gardener's beds turn the shade of ash, then the koi, then the gardener's own blue sleeves. It is not poison, the Ministry says. It is something worse and more patient. Up the slope, the {og_passage} is weeping the rain out of its crack.

choices.text: Hold an umbrella of qi over the gardens

effects.log: You keep the rain off one garden for a day and a night. One garden stays red and gold.

choices.text: Catch a cup of the rain and study it

effects.log: It is memory, you think, of a world that is gone. It leaves your fingertips pale for a month.

choices.text: Take the gardener to your isle

effects.log: He brings one cutting of a peony. It grows, slowly, and it is red.

events.text: The Jade Court rings the Bell of the Nine Heavens for the first time in an age. Ministers arrive in mismatched robes, one with a sleeve still pinned. The proclamation is short: the {og_passage} is breached, the gods above are fighting, and every immortal of standing is asked to report to the Ninefold Watch. Asked, the Court says. It means told.

choices.text: Report to the Watch at once

effects.log: You give your name at the Watch-house. The clerk writes it with a hand that shakes only a little.

choices.text: Argue for sending envoys up to the gods

effects.log: You argue well. The Court sends three envoys. None comes back, but word does: the gods are already there.

choices.text: Slip back to your isle before roll-call

effects.log: You are not missed today. You will be, later, by someone who notices such things.

events.text: A captain of the Ninefold Watch falls through your roof, quite literally, in a shower of tiles. His white coat is grey to the elbow, and he is laughing in the way people laugh when they have stopped being afraid. 'They came up the Stair singing,' he tells your ceiling. 'Singing, in a language with no word for tomorrow.'

choices.text: Tend him yourself, with your best pills

effects.log: Your pills bring the colour back to his arm by morning. He owes you a life and says so, gravely.

choices.text: Ask him what they look like

effects.log: Like people drawn by someone who heard of people once, he says. You write it down.

choices.text: Carry him to the Lotus Infirmary

effects.log: You fly him there at speed. The Infirmary is already full, and makes room.

events.text: From the high terrace of your isle you see the whole thing at once: the {og_passage} glowing like a cracked lantern, and the factions' cloud-barges moving in two great streams, one toward the Stair and one away from it. The banners are mixed in both. For once, nobody on the Isles can tell who is who by colour alone.

choices.text: Join the stream going toward the Stair

effects.log: You fly with the barges going in. The faces aboard are frightened and certain, which is the best kind.

choices.text: Hail the barges going away and ask why

effects.log: They have children aboard, and old masters, and libraries. You help them find berths on the far isles.

choices.text: Watch, and count the barges

effects.log: You count. You will remember which banners went where, and so will the Isles.

events.text: A little girl on the lowest landing of the Isles says the crack in the {og_passage} is calling everyone by name. It is very kind, she says. It knows her name, and her mother's, and yours. She is not frightened at all, and that is what frightens you, because from where you stand you can hear it too.

choices.text: Cover her ears, and lead her away

effects.log: You walk her to the far side of the isle. The voice gets thinner with every step, and then it is only wind.

choices.text: Listen to what it says of you

effects.log: It says your name, and then the names of everyone you have lost, as if offering them back. You stop listening.

choices.text: Sing over it, loud and out of tune

effects.log: You sing a ferry song badly. The girl laughs and sings too, and the voice gives up on you both.

events.text: Three barges of salt-farmers from the lower cloud-flats tie up at your landing in the night, without asking. Their flats are grey now, and their salt tastes of nothing. They have brought their goats, their grandmothers and a very good kettle. The eldest of them asks for nothing, and keeps looking at your empty guest-halls.

choices.text: Open the guest-halls to them

effects.log: The halls fill with goats and grandmothers. The kettle is, in fact, very good.

choices.text: Send them on to the Ministry camps

effects.log: They untie and go. The kettle goes with them, and so does your good name on that landing.

choices.text: Take their young ones into the Watch

effects.log: The young ones go to the Watch with spears. The old ones stay on your landing, and never quite forgive you.

events.text: She comes up the Stair alone, through the crack, before the Watch can stop her: a woman from a dimension that no longer exists, in clothes of a fashion nobody will ever wear again. She speaks a tongue with no future tense. She has a pressed flower in a book, the last flower of her world, and she shows it to you as if asking whether it is worth anything.

choices.text: Give her a room and a window

effects.log: She lives in your west room for a hundred years and learns your word for tomorrow. She uses it often.

choices.text: Hand her to the Ministry examiners

effects.log: The Ministry is careful with strangers from the crack. You do not hear of her again.

choices.text: Ask her to teach the Watch what she knows

effects.log: She teaches the Watch how her world fell. They listen very hard. It helps them.

events.text: A whole little isle drifts up out of the grey below, pushed loose by the breach, with a village still on it: thirty roofs, a shrine, a dog asleep on a step. It bumps gently against your landing like a boat. The village headman climbs across with his hat in his hands. 'We would like to tie up,' he says, 'if it is no trouble.'

choices.text: Moor their isle beside yours

effects.log: You lash the two isles together with qi-rope. The dog wakes, considers you, and goes back to sleep.

choices.text: Push the isle gently on toward the far reaches

effects.log: It drifts away toward the far reaches. The headman waves his hat until you cannot see it.

choices.text: Moor it, if its men stand watch for the Isles

effects.log: The men take the watch. The village keeps its roofs, and you keep a debt of service you did not entirely earn.

events.text: The Ninefold Watch sends you its orphans: fourteen children of fallen watchmen, in coats too big for them, holding hands in a line. The Watch-house cannot keep them; the front is too close. The smallest one has her father's whistle round her neck, and blows it every time someone says the word 'Stair'.

choices.text: Take all fourteen in

effects.log: Your isle is noisy for a century. You learn to sleep through whistles.

choices.text: Send them on to the Celestial Ministries

effects.log: The Ministries take them in a long, polite barge. The whistle grows fainter over the water.

choices.text: Train the oldest ones for the Watch

effects.log: The oldest four go back to the Watch with their fathers' coats taken in. They are very good.

events.text: The refugees at your landing look right in every way but one: their shadows are a hand too long, and fall the wrong way at noon. They are polite, tired and grateful. A watchman whispers that the Unborn send scouts in borrowed shapes. The tired mother at the front of the line hears him, and holds her child a little closer.

choices.text: Shelter them, shadows and all

effects.log: You give them the east hall. Nothing comes of the shadows but a long and peculiar friendship.

choices.text: Turn them away, to be safe

effects.log: They go without arguing. You spend some nights wondering what was true, and get no answer.

choices.text: Shelter them under the Watch's eye

effects.log: They shelter under guard. They are only refugees, as it turns out, and they know they were watched.

events.text: An old scholar from a dead world comes to you carrying a box. Inside, folded smaller than seems possible, is the last library of his dimension: forty thousand books, and a recipe for a soup nobody alive has tasted. He needs a dry room and a few hundred years. He is quite sure the box will outlive him, and quite calm about it.

choices.text: Give the library a room in your hall

effects.log: The box unfolds into three rooms. You read in them often, and once you make the soup.

choices.text: Send him to the Cloud Library instead

effects.log: The Cloud Library is full and turns him away. You hear later that he found a cave.

choices.text: Ask him for the books on how his world fell

effects.log: He gives the Watch the war-books and keeps the poems. It is a fair bargain, and a sad one.

events.text: The Lotus Infirmary has run out of beds, then floors, then courtyards. The Celestial Ministries send a circular to every isle of standing asking for room for the wounded of the Stair: watchmen, ferrymen, a goat-herd who held a landing alone with a crook. The circular is signed by twelve ministers, which means nobody is in charge.

choices.text: Turn your training yard into a ward

effects.log: Your yard fills with cots. You learn the names of the wounded, and some of them learn yours.

choices.text: Send back a polite letter saying you have no room

effects.log: The letter is filed. It will be read again, one day, by someone with a list.

choices.text: Take the ones who can still fight

effects.log: You take the walking wounded and put spears in their hands. They mend faster, angry.

events.text: Of all the isles they could have come to, the refugees of the Copper Reach come to yours. Their faction has hated your hall for three hundred years. Their elder bows to the floor and says nothing about the old quarrel, the stolen manual or the duel on the Bridge of Reeds. Their isle is grey to the roots. They have nowhere else that would take them.

choices.text: Open your gate to your old enemies

effects.log: They come in. The quarrel does not end, but it learns to share a kitchen.

choices.text: Turn them away; old debts are old debts

effects.log: They go. The other isles hear of it, and remember it in your favour and against you in equal parts.

choices.text: Take them in, and put their fighters on the Stair

effects.log: Their fighters go to the Stair under your banner. The elder thanks you with a face like a shut door.

events.text: The Ninefold Watch is holding the top landing of the {og_passage} with spears, arrays and stubbornness, and the grey things are climbing out of the crack faster than the spears can turn. Warden Lan Ji sends runners to every isle with the same three words: come or don't. There is no third thing written on the paper.

choices.text: Go up, and stand on the landing with the Watch

ok.log: You hold the left flank till sunset. The grey goes back down the crack in a long, angry sigh.

fail.log: They come too fast. You are carried off the landing on a door, grey to the knees.

choices.text: Stay on your isle; the Watch has its orders

effects.log: The landing holds without you, barely. Lan Ji does not write to you again.

events.text: The Bridge of Reeds is the only way from the Stair to the Ministry Isles that a barge cannot take, and the Unborn have found it. Something tall and patient is crossing it a step at a time, and each step leaves the reeds behind it grey. A dozen young immortals stand at the far end with their swords out, waiting for someone older to arrive.

choices.text: Be the someone older

roll.foeName: the walker on the Bridge of Reeds

ok.log: You meet it in the middle of the bridge and send it back over the edge. The reeds are green again by spring.

fail.log: It is stronger than it looks, and it looks strong. You are thrown back to the far end, and the young ones hold it while you rise.

choices.text: Cut the bridge, and let it fall

effects.log: The bridge falls into the clouds, and the thing with it. The Ministry Isles are an island now, in every sense.

events.text: The Celestial Ministries are moving their archives off the Ministry Isles by barge: ten thousand years of records, the Jade Court's Rolls, the deeds of every isle. The barges are slow and low in the water, and grey shapes have been seen in the clouds beneath them. The Ministry asks for an escort and pays in honour, which is all it has left to pay in.

choices.text: Fly escort over the archive barges

ok.log: You drive them off three times before the far isles. Every scroll arrives dry.

fail.log: One barge goes down. Its scrolls scatter on the Cloud Sea like leaves, and you go into the clouds after them and come out half-drowned.

choices.text: Let the factions escort their own records

effects.log: The factions do. Some records arrive, and some arrive a little changed.

events.text: The Lotus Isles are under siege. Not by an army, but by a slow grey tide that comes up the slopes each night and goes down a little less each morning. Inside the ring, the gardeners are still watering their beds out of habit. The captain of the isle's guard sends you a single peony, white now, with a note: one more night.

choices.text: Break the ring before nightfall

roll.foeName: the grey tide on the Lotus slopes

ok.log: You cut through the ring at dusk and hold the gap till dawn. The tide goes down and does not come back.

fail.log: The tide closes behind you. You fight your way out at dawn with the guard captain on your back, and the isle is lost to the grey.

choices.text: Send them a barge to flee in, and no more

effects.log: The gardeners come out on your barge with their seeds in their sleeves. The isle goes grey behind them.

events.text: A grey fleet comes out of the crack in the {og_passage}: cloud-barges, or the memory of them, rowed by things that have learned rowing from watching. They steer for the Ministry Isles in perfect silence. The factions' fleets are still arguing about who leads. A gap opens between them where somebody could stand.

choices.text: Stand in the gap, alone if need be

ok.log: You break the lead barge on your own blade and the rest lose their way. The factions stop arguing to cheer.

fail.log: The fleet goes round you like water round a stone. You are caught in the wake and come home with a cracked qi-sea.

choices.text: Go and settle the argument instead

effects.log: You get the factions to agree on a leader. It is not you. The fleet is turned, late, at a cost.

events.text: The Watch's night patrol has not come back from the middle landings of the {og_passage}. Their lantern can still be seen down there, swinging slowly, far below, as if someone were signalling or simply could not let go. Lan Ji is gathering volunteers. She has eleven. She would like twelve.

choices.text: Be the twelfth, and go down the Stair

roll.foeName: the dark of the middle landings

ok.log: You find the patrol in a ring around their lantern, alive and grey and very glad to see you. You bring every one of them up.

fail.log: The dark is thicker than any of you guessed. You come back with the lantern and four of the patrol, and you do not talk about it.

choices.text: Hold the top of the Stair while they go

effects.log: You hold the top landing all night with the lamps lit. Eleven go down. Eleven come back, with the patrol.

events.text: A grey swarm has settled on the lower isles like starlings on a field: thousands of small things, no bigger than cats, nibbling. Where they nibble, a spirit-stone vein goes cold and a qi-spring stops. The miners have locked themselves in the mines. Somebody needs to scatter them before the cold reaches the roots of the Isles.

choices.text: Go down and scatter the swarm

ok.log: You go through them like wind through a field. The springs run again by the end of the week.

fail.log: There are more of them than there is of you. You come back with cold fingers and the swarm only thinned.

choices.text: Seal the springs, and let the swarm starve

effects.log: You seal the springs with arrays. The swarm starves, slowly, and so do the miners' wages.

events.text: The Unborn have a lieutenant on the Isles: a thing in a long coat that calls itself the Usher and bows to everyone it meets. It has been seen at three landings this month, and three landings have gone grey. Tonight it is at the Hall of the Rising Pine, bowing to the doorman. The doorman, they say, is bowing back.

choices.text: Go to the Hall, and do not bow

ok.log: It bows to you. You do not bow back. It is gone by the second exchange, coat and all, and the doorman blinks awake.

fail.log: It bows, and you find yourself half bowing too, and by the time you are upright it has struck. You leave the Hall on a stretcher.

choices.text: Warn every landing to shut its doors

effects.log: You ride all night with warnings. Doors shut. The Usher finds them shut, and goes back down, for now.

events.text: The Ninefold Watch's last line is a row of old arrays at the top of the {og_passage}, built before your grandteacher's grandteacher, and they are failing one by one like lamps in the wind. The array-masters need someone to stand in front of them for a day and a night while they rebuild. Someone who will not move.

choices.text: Stand before the arrays, and do not move

ok.log: You stand a day and a night. When the arrays wake behind you, the light goes down the Stair like a broom.

fail.log: You move. You do not mean to, but you are thrown, and two arrays go out for good before the masters finish.

choices.text: Give the array-masters your qi instead

effects.log: You pour your qi into their brushes. The arrays wake, and you sleep for a week.

events.text: A single grey thing has come up the Stair and made a home in an empty pavilion on your own isle. It does not attack. It sits at the table and looks at the teacups as if trying to remember what they were for. Your servants have stopped going into the east garden. One of them heard it humming a lullaby in no language at all.

choices.text: Go in and drive it out

roll.foeName: the guest in the east pavilion

ok.log: It does not fight much. It goes, at last, back to the crack, and you find it has left the teacups in a neat row.

fail.log: It fights more than you expected, sadly and well. You win back the pavilion in the end, and lose the use of an arm for a season.

choices.text: Leave it be, and close the east garden

effects.log: The east garden stays closed. The humming goes on for years, very quietly.

events.text: The Jade Court's own stair, the white one from the Ministry Isles to the Court, has a grey thing on every hundredth step, sitting like a pilgrim. Ministers have stopped going to work. The Court cannot meet. There is talk that if the Court cannot meet, the factions will stop pretending there is one, and then the Isles will have two wars instead of one.

choices.text: Climb the white stair, step by step

roll.foeName: the pilgrims on the white stair

ok.log: You clear the stair by noon. The Court meets at dusk, late, and the first item is your name.

fail.log: You get halfway. The pilgrims close behind you, and you come down the long way, through the clouds, in a bad state.

choices.text: Talk the factions into meeting elsewhere

effects.log: The factions meet in a tea-house. It is not the Court, but it is not a second war either.

events.text: After a month of fighting at the {og_passage}, a quiet comes. The grey stops climbing. The Watch is too tired to cheer. Then, at dusk, something comes up the Stair that is not a swarm or a pilgrim, but a single figure with a spear made of the light of a dead sun, and every array on the top landing goes out at once.

choices.text: Meet it at the top of the Stair

roll.foeName: the spear of the dead sun

ok.log: It is the last of them, for now, and the strongest. You break the spear across your knee in the end. The arrays light again.

fail.log: You meet it, and it is too much. It goes back down the Stair of its own choosing, laughing, and you are carried home.

choices.text: Fall back with the Watch to the second landing

effects.log: You fall back. The figure stands on the top landing for a night, looking at the Isles, and then goes down.

events.text: A herald climbs up out of the crack and walks straight to your landing as if it had an appointment. It wears a coat sewn from the flags of eaten worlds and carries a scroll it does not need to read. 'The Hollow Dao,' it says, 'sends its compliments to the Isles, and asks them to be still. It will not take long.'

choices.text: Answer it with your blade

roll.foeName: the herald in the coat of flags

ok.log: It did not expect an answer. You send it back down with its coat in rags and its compliments unsent.

fail.log: It answers you with something that is not a blade and not a word. You wake on your own floor at noon.

choices.text: Let it read its scroll, and say nothing

effects.log: It reads. The words are very patient and very cold. It leaves, and you remember every one.

events.text: The herald comes to the Jade Court itself, in daylight, and the guards let it pass because it bows so very correctly. It asks for a list: every isle, every faction, every immortal of note. 'For the accounts,' it explains, 'so nothing is wasted.' The ministers look at each other. Somebody is going to have to say no, and they are all looking at you.

choices.text: Say no, and make it stick

ok.log: You say no in the old way. It leaves with an empty book and a crooked hat.

fail.log: You say no. It writes your name first, in very good ink, before you throw it out the window. It does not go far.

choices.text: Give it a list of the dead, and nothing else

effects.log: You give it the names of the fallen. It reads them aloud with real care, and goes away, and you are not sure who won.

events.text: A herald sits down beside you at the tea-house on the White Stairs and orders two cups. It is courteous, almost shy. It explains that it was once the herald of a pantheon that is now a story, and that it does this work now because it does not know any other. It asks whether the tea here is good. It is waiting for something.

choices.text: Rise and fight it here, among the cups

ok.log: It does not want to fight, and fights badly. When it falls, it thanks you, which you did not expect.

fail.log: It fights very well for something shy. The tea-house is in pieces and so are you.

choices.text: Drink the tea with it, and ask about its pantheon

effects.log: It tells you the names of its gods, one by one. When it leaves, it leaves the second cup untouched for you.

events.text: The herald does not climb the Stair. It is simply there one morning, standing on the water of the Cloud Sea below your isle, and calling up to you by a name you have not used since you were mortal. It knows the town you came from. It knows the river. It describes them lovingly and in detail, as a cook describes a meal.

choices.text: Go down to the water and silence it

roll.foeName: the herald on the Cloud Sea

ok.log: You walk on the water to meet it. It sinks into the clouds mid-word, and your old name goes with it.

fail.log: It keeps talking while it fights. You lose the fight and, for a month, the sound of your own river.

choices.text: Close your shutters on it

effects.log: You close them. It calls until sunset. You do not sleep, and in the morning it is gone.

events.text: The herald has brought a gift to the Watch-house: a spear of the Ninefold Watch, white and good as new, belonging to a watchman who went down the Stair a month ago and did not come back. It sets it on the step with real gentleness. 'He asked us to return it,' it says. 'He asked us for nothing else, so we gave him nothing else.'

choices.text: Take up the spear, and drive the herald off with it

ok.log: The spear knows its way. The herald goes over the edge of the landing and does not come back for its manners.

fail.log: The spear is heavy with grief and so are you. The herald steps round you and goes on its way.

choices.text: Carry the spear to the watchman's mother

effects.log: You carry it to her yourself. She keeps it by her door, and you visit her every year.

events.text: Two heralds come up the Stair together, arguing. One wants to announce the Hollow Dao to the Isles in full, with all its titles. The other thinks this is vulgar and wants to announce only the date. They ask you, very politely, to settle it, since you seem to be an immortal of taste. Both of them have swords. Neither of them has put them away.

choices.text: Settle it with your own sword

ok.log: You settle it, and both of them. The Isles hear neither the titles nor the date.

fail.log: They stop arguing to fight you, together, and it turns out they are very good together. You lose.

choices.text: Ask them to come back when they agree

effects.log: They go down the Stair still arguing. They have not agreed yet, as far as anyone knows.

events.text: The {og_passage} holds. The word comes down from the gods in a single plain sentence, and the Isles go quiet with relief. The crack is closing. The grey rain has stopped. On every landing people come out of doors and look up as if they had never seen a sky. Warden Lan Ji sits on the top step and takes off her helmet for the first time in a year.

choices.text: Sit beside her on the step

effects.log: You sit. Neither of you says anything for an hour. It is the best hour of the year.

choices.text: Go round the landings, thanking every watchman

effects.log: It takes a week. By the end of it you know every name on the Stair.

events.text: The Ministries hold a feast for the holding of the Stair, and it is not a very good feast, because the Isles have eaten through most of their stores. There is thin soup and a great deal of wine. Someone has written the names of the fallen on a long cloth along the hall, and nobody can look at it and nobody can look away.

choices.text: Read every name on the cloth aloud

effects.log: You read for two hours. The hall goes quiet, and then someone begins to sing.

choices.text: Raise a cup to the gods who held it above

effects.log: The hall raises its cups with you. Far above, you like to think, someone feels it.

events.text: In the morning after the Stair holds, the peonies on the Lotus Isles open red. Not all of them, and not the old ones: just the new shoots, from seeds the gardeners carried through the siege in their sleeves. The gardener you once sheltered brings you the first flower in a cup of water, and does not say a word, because none is needed.

choices.text: Plant it in your own courtyard

effects.log: It takes. Every spring after, your courtyard is the reddest on the isle.

choices.text: Give it to the Watch-house

effects.log: It sits in the Watch-house window for years. The watchmen water it in turns, very seriously.

events.text: The {og_passage} is whole again, but the Isles are not. Grey patches remain in old gardens; one landing still hums at night. A council of factions meets to decide who pays to mend what. It is the first time in three thousand years that every faction has sat at one table, and they argue so happily that the ministers stop trying to keep order.

choices.text: Argue too, for the lower landings

effects.log: You win the lower landings a good share. The salt-farmers send you a goat in thanks.

choices.text: Let them argue, and go to the Stair to look

effects.log: You walk the whole Stair. It is healing, slowly, like a bone.

events.text: The word comes down from above: the {og_passage} has broken. The gods could not hold it. The crack is not closing now; it is a door, and it is open, and the Ministries are already writing new maps with the Stair drawn in grey. Warden Lan Ji has not come back from the top landing. Her helmet has.

choices.text: Go up and find her

effects.log: You find her at the bottom of the top flight, alive, and grey to the shoulder. She asks for her helmet first.

choices.text: Take the helmet to the Watch-house and hang it up

effects.log: You hang it where every watchman will pass it. The Watch, smaller now, swears by it.

events.text: The Stair has fallen, and the Isles learn what that means in a single week. The grey does not rush. It seeps. A spring here, a garden there, a landing whose stones go soft. The factions blame each other in public and help each other in private. Your own isle is still bright, for now. You can see the grey from your terrace.

choices.text: Shore up your arrays, and take in what you can

effects.log: Your isle becomes a lantern on the edge of the grey. People row toward it at night.

choices.text: Join the factions' council of the fallen Stair

effects.log: The council is long and tired. It decides very little. You are on it, which is something.

events.text: When the {og_passage} broke, the sound reached the farthest isles: a long, low note like the last string of an instrument going. Since then the Cloud Sea has been quieter. The cranes fly lower. The young immortals, who were born after the last great war, keep asking what happens next, and the old ones keep finding errands to run.

choices.text: Tell the young ones the truth

effects.log: You tell them. It is hard to hear. They take it better than the old ones did.

choices.text: Tell them a story of the Stair before it fell

effects.log: You tell it well. They will tell it to their own young, and it will be true in the telling.

events.text: The Jade Court sits in the evening of the fall, and nobody speaks for a long time. At last an old minister stands and reads out the list of isles under the grey. It is longer than anyone expected and shorter than anyone feared. When she finishes, she folds the paper and asks the Court what it intends to do now. Nobody has an answer. Everybody looks round.

choices.text: Stand and give them one

effects.log: You say: hold what is left, and mend what can be mended. It is not much. They write it down.

choices.text: Say nothing, and go home to your isle

effects.log: You go home. The Court sits until dawn without you, and agrees on nothing.

events.text: The {og_passage} has stood broken for longer than this life remembers, and the Isles have learned to live beside it like a village beside a volcano. Grey creeps in at the edges of things. Every year a few more springs go cold. Every year a few more barges come up through the crack, full of faces from worlds that are gone.

choices.text: Go down to the crack and count the barges

effects.log: You count forty in a month. You take the count to the Ministries, who already knew.

choices.text: Plant a bright garden at the edge of the grey

effects.log: Your garden holds the grey back by three paces. Three paces is a good deal.

choices.text: Look away, as the Isles have learned to

effects.log: You look away. It is easier than you thought, and that is worse.

events.text: The grey moss reached your isle this spring. It came in on the soles of a pilgrim's sandals, the gardeners say, and now it is in the cracks of your courtyard, soft and patient. Where it grows, qi thins. You can scrape it out, and it comes back. Your oldest servant, who has kept this hall for six hundred years, has started counting the cracks.

choices.text: Burn it out with your own qi, crack by crack

effects.log: It takes a season. The courtyard is clean, and you are thinner in your meridians.

choices.text: Study it, and learn how it grows

effects.log: It grows toward warmth and away from song. You teach the servants to sing at their work.

choices.text: Let it be; it is everywhere now

effects.log: It spreads. Your servant stops counting, and you both pretend not to notice.

events.text: The Celestial Ministries ration spirit stones now, because the broken {og_passage} has been bleeding qi into the grey for centuries. Every isle gets a share by standing. Your share is generous. At the ration-house on the lowest landing, you see a line of refugees from a dead world who get nothing at all, because they have no standing.

choices.text: Give half your share to the line

effects.log: The line is grateful and silent. You are thinner, and you sleep well.

choices.text: Petition the Ministries to give them standing

effects.log: The petition goes round twelve ministers. It comes back with eleven seals and one question mark.

choices.text: Take your share and go

effects.log: You take it. Nobody in the line looks at you. That is somehow worse than if they had.

events.text: There is a new isle in the Cloud Sea. It came up through the crack in the broken Stair a hundred years ago, and it is full of people from a dimension the Hollow Dao finished eating. They have built a town there out of things that drifted up with them. They call it Afterward. The factions call it a problem, and want it moved.

choices.text: Visit Afterward, and speak for it at Court

effects.log: You speak at Court for a town of strangers. It is allowed to stay. They name a street for you.

choices.text: Visit, and learn what they know of the Unborn

effects.log: They know a great deal. They have watched it from the other side. You take notes until your hand aches.

choices.text: Leave it to the factions

effects.log: The factions argue for a century. Afterward stays, in the end, out of sheer stubbornness.

events.text: A sickness of the grey is going through the lower isles: it makes people forget small things first, names of flowers, the way home, then larger. The Lotus Infirmary calls it the Thinning. The cure, if there is one, will come from someone patient enough to sit with the sick and learn what the grey takes first. The Infirmary is short of patient people.

choices.text: Sit with the sick, and learn

effects.log: You sit with them a year. You learn that it takes music last. You teach the Infirmary to play for them.

choices.text: Brew pills for the Infirmary instead

effects.log: Your pills slow it. It is not a cure. It is time, which is the next best thing.

choices.text: Stay away from the lower isles

effects.log: You stay away. You forget, now and then, the name of a flower. You tell yourself it is age.

events.text: The factions have started to fight over the bright isles that are left. It began with a quarrel over a spring, and now there are barges with drawn swords in the straits, and a Ministry runner was turned away from a landing at sword's point. Beyond them all, the grey waits. It does not need to fight. It only needs the Isles to.

choices.text: Stand between the barges in the strait

effects.log: You stand between them for a day. They put up their swords, grumbling, and go home.

choices.text: Take the matter to the Jade Court

effects.log: The Court rules. Both factions ignore the ruling, and keep the peace anyway, out of shame.

choices.text: Back the faction nearer to you

effects.log: They win the spring. The other faction remembers, as the grey does.

events.text: Every hundred years, on the anniversary of the Stair's fall, the Isles hold a night of lamps. Each household sends a lantern down the broken {og_passage} into the grey, one for every world the Hollow Dao has eaten that anyone can still name. There are more lanterns each time. This year the line of them goes so far down that nobody can see the end.

choices.text: Send a lantern for a world nobody named

effects.log: You write 'for the one nobody remembers' on yours. Others see it, and copy it.

choices.text: Walk down the Stair beside the lanterns

effects.log: You walk down as far as the grey allows. It allows further than last time. You come back cold.

choices.text: Stay up on the terrace and watch

effects.log: You watch them go down, a river of small lights. It is beautiful, and you hate that it is.

events.text: A child born on Afterward, the refugee isle, has been accepted to an immortal academy, the first of her people to be. The academy elders are nervous. Her shadow is a hand too long. On the first day, the other students will not sit beside her. She sits very straight, alone, at the end of the bench, and waits to be taught.

choices.text: Go to the academy and sit beside her yourself

effects.log: You sit beside her for a lesson. The next day, two students do. The day after, the bench is full.

choices.text: Offer to teach her privately

effects.log: She learns faster than anyone you have taught. She is very kind about it.

choices.text: Leave it to the academy

effects.log: The academy does its best. She stays, alone on her bench, and grows very strong.

events.text: A stranger has been asking about you on the White Stairs: polite, tall, with a face that does not quite settle. It asks which isle is yours, what you eat, whether you have any old memories of a war in heaven. The tea-seller who tells you this shivers. 'It said it was looking for an old friend,' she says. 'It said it the way a cat says mouse.'

choices.text: Find it before it finds you

ok.log: You find it in a tea-house and it is not a stranger: it is an Unborn in a borrowed face. You send it back to wherever it came from.

fail.log: It finds you first. It looks at you a long while, and says 'not yet', and leaves you on the floor of your own hall.

choices.text: Leave the Isles for a while, quietly

effects.log: You go to the far reaches for ten years. The stranger stops asking. It does not stop looking.

events.text: You wake in the night with a taste of ash and an old, old certainty: something is in your hall that remembers you from before this life. It is sitting in your chair. In the dark it looks almost like you. 'You killed my Dao,' it says, without anger, the way a widow states a fact. 'I have come to see what you are now.'

choices.text: Show it, with your blade

ok.log: You show it. It leaves through the wall, satisfied or frightened, you cannot tell which.

fail.log: It sees what you are now, and is not impressed. It goes, and leaves you with a cold that takes a year to leave.

choices.text: Light a lamp, and ask what it wants

effects.log: It wants nothing. It wanted to see. The lamp makes it small, and it goes.

events.text: The Ministry of Stars sends you a private note: a spark has been seen moving against the stars, low over your isle, three nights running. It is not a star. It is following your qi, the astronomers think, as a hound follows a scent. They are very sorry to trouble you. They wanted you to know that someone was looking.

choices.text: Climb to your roof and wait for it

effects.log: It comes at the third hour and hangs above you. You stare back until it goes. It does not come again.

choices.text: Hide your qi under a heavy array

effects.log: The array is heavy and dull to live under. The spark circles, confused, and moves on.

choices.text: Thank the astronomers, and ignore it

effects.log: You ignore it. It does not ignore you, but it does not come closer either.

events.text: A young immortal of the Watch comes to you with a strange confession: a voice in a dream offered them great strength if they would only bring it a lock of your hair. They refused. They are frightened that they almost did not. They say the voice sounded old, and hurt, and as if it had once lost everything to someone very like you.

choices.text: Thank them, and teach them to guard their dreams

effects.log: You teach them a sleeping array. The voice does not come back to them. It may come to someone else.

choices.text: Ask them to say yes next time, and set a trap

effects.log: They say yes. The trap closes on a shadow that screams like wind and is gone. The young one sleeps better.

choices.text: Cut your hair short, and laugh about it

effects.log: You cut it. The young one laughs too. It is the first time they have laughed in a month.

events.text: The war above is in one of its long silences. The Stair is quiet, the Watch has gone back to playing chess on the top landing, and the grey patches in old gardens are, if anything, smaller. People on the Isles have started saying 'after the war' as if it were a real time. It might be. Nobody has asked the gods.

choices.text: Climb to the top landing and play a game of chess

effects.log: Lan Ji beats you three times. She has had a lot of practice on that landing.

choices.text: Use the quiet to train

effects.log: You train in the quiet. It is good quiet for training: watchful, and never quite still.

events.text: A refugee from a dead world opens a noodle stall on the White Stairs. The noodles are terrible. The broth is a recipe from a dimension that no longer exists, and it tastes of a sea no one will see again. There is a line round the corner every day, mostly immortals who will not say why they come.

choices.text: Join the line, every day

effects.log: You eat a great many bad noodles. The broth is worth it, every time.

choices.text: Help her get better flour

effects.log: The noodles get better. She is very pleased, and the broth stays exactly the same.

events.text: In a quiet year the Ministries publish a list, at last, of the worlds the Hollow Dao is known to have eaten. It is a short book. It is a short book only because so few worlds left anyone behind to remember them. You find a copy in the Cloud Library and read it at a corner table. You are not the only one reading it, and nobody turns the pages fast.

choices.text: Read it all, every name

effects.log: You read until closing. You remember more of the names than you would expect.

choices.text: Read until you cannot, and go for a walk

effects.log: You walk round the isle twice. The sea is bright and here, and you are glad of it.

events.text: The young immortals of your isle have a new game: one is the Unborn, one is the Watch, and the rest are the Isles, who run about shrieking. You watch from the terrace. The Unborn always loses. The Watch always wins. In the version they play, the gods come down at the end and everyone has dumplings. You have no intention of correcting it.

choices.text: Come down and play the gods

effects.log: You play the gods. You bring real dumplings. It is a triumph.

choices.text: Leave them to it, and smile

effects.log: You leave them to it. The game goes on for years and changes rules every week.

events.text: Warden Lan Ji is retiring. Nine hundred years at the top of the Stair, and she is going to a small isle with a garden and no knocking. She asks you to come to the top landing one last time, and stand the night watch with her. Nothing knocks. Toward dawn she says, very quietly, that she misses it.

choices.text: Tell her you will keep the watch sometimes

effects.log: You keep it sometimes, after. The Stair is quieter with you there. Or you imagine so.

choices.text: Give her your best tea for the garden isle

effects.log: She takes it and laughs. She sends you a letter every year, about her peonies.

events.text: A ferryman of the Cloud Sea brings you an odd catch in his net: a little glass bead with a whole sky inside it, stars and all, from some world gone before ours had a name. It is warm. It is all that is left. He thinks it should go to someone who will keep it safe, and he has decided, without asking, that this is you.

choices.text: Keep it on your desk, always

effects.log: It sits on your desk. On bad nights you look at its stars, and they help.

choices.text: Give it to the Cloud Library

effects.log: The Library makes a case for it. Children press their faces to the glass all day.

events.text: The factions hold the first friendly contest of arts since the Stair breached, on a meadow isle where the grey never reached. Nobody keeps score very seriously. A watchman wins the archery and cries. Somebody's grandteacher wins the poetry. You are asked, as an immortal of standing, to give out the prizes, which are mostly cakes.

choices.text: Enter the swordplay, for fun

effects.log: You lose to a girl of ninety in the third round, and laugh about it for a week.

choices.text: Give out the cakes with great ceremony

effects.log: You give them out with perfect gravity. It is the most popular thing you do all century.

events.text: Some nights, in the quiet years, you still hear it: the old note of the {og_passage}, low and patient, like a breath held under the floor of heaven. The gods above are holding. Down here the Isles are mending. But you were here when it broke, or nearly broke, and a part of you is always listening.

choices.text: Go and sit on the Stair till morning

effects.log: You sit till morning. The note is only a note. It does not change. You go home and sleep.

choices.text: Teach yourself not to listen

effects.log: It takes a decade. You learn it, mostly. On bad nights you remember why you learned it.

events.text: On the White Stairs there is a statue nobody remembers commissioning: a god with no face, holding a broken sun. The Isles call it the One Who Ended It. The plaque says only that a god of this heaven fought the Hollow Dao to its end and won. Pilgrims leave peonies at its feet. When you pass it, the peonies turn toward you like flowers to the light.

choices.text: Stop, and lay a peony of your own

effects.log: You lay it with the others. It is strange to honour yourself, and stranger not to know you are.

choices.text: Walk on, a little faster

effects.log: You walk on. The peonies follow you with their faces till you turn the corner.

events.text: Grandmothers on the lower landings tell a story to frightened children: once the sky had a hole in it, and a hungry thing came through, and a god went out alone to the edge of everything and ate it back. The story is wrong in most details. You know this, somehow, the way you know your own handwriting. You do not know how you know.

choices.text: Sit and listen to the story

effects.log: The children ask you if it is true. You say yes, without thinking. The grandmother looks at you sharply.

choices.text: Correct one small detail

effects.log: You say the god did not go alone. The grandmother nods slowly and puts it in next time.

events.text: In the Cloud Library, in a locked room the archivist opens only for you, is a scroll of the war in heaven. It ends with the Hollow Dao's death, and the name of the god who ended it is scratched out, not by an enemy, but as the custom is for those who chose to be reborn. The scratching is in a hand very like yours.

choices.text: Read the scroll to the end

effects.log: You read it. A great tiredness comes over you, and then a great quiet, and you sleep in the Library.

choices.text: Close it, and leave it locked

effects.log: You close it. Some things are better as stories. The archivist bows to you, very low, on your way out.

events.text: A refugee isle that came up through the old crack in the Stair, long ago, still keeps a feast for the day the Hollow Dao died. On that day they cook the food of their own dead world and set an empty place at the head of the table for the god who ended it. This year their elder sees you passing and, for no reason they can name, invites you in.

choices.text: Take the empty place

effects.log: You take it. The elder serves you first. Nobody says why, and the food tastes of a sea you somehow remember.

choices.text: Sit at the foot instead

effects.log: You sit at the foot. The head place stays empty. That feels right, and the elder thinks so too.
